source_name: IVSZ – Digitális Vállalkozások Szövetsége (fintech working group and member base)
why_relevant: IVSZ is the ICT/digital-business association; its Fintech Munkacsoport publishes trend positions on the fintech and banking sector, and its rolling 'új tagok' announcements enumerate technology vendors (CRM, cybersecurity, insurtech brokers, customer-service digitalisation) entering the market — precisely the supplier-side competitor set that bank-only member lists miss.

source_name: AmCham Hungary – Membership Directory (financial services members)
why_relevant: Bilingual member directory with per-company profile pages for banks operating in Hungary (OTP Bank, K&H Bank, ING Bank N.V. Hungary Branch, Deutsche Bank Hungarian Branch observed). Adds branch-office and foreign-parent entities that domestic associations under-represent, and AmCham committees/Board pages map senior financial-sector executives.

Quarterly and annual factoring-market statistics (series observed from 2019 to 2026; e.g. Q1 2025 financing volume >HUF 486bn, +28–41% y/y). Factoring volumes are a leading indicator of SME credit demand and of non-bank working-capital competition against banks.

source_name: MAKISZ – Magyar Követeléskezelők és Üzleti Információt Szolgáltatók Szövetsége
why_relevant: Debt-purchase and business-information association; ~41 members reported purchasing ~HUF 320bn of receivables (2020) and managing ~HUF 500bn. Enumerates the receivables-management and credit-bureau vendor set that sits downstream of every bank and leasing house, and runs sector conferences (e.g. on leasing-portfolio collections).

source_name: MABISZ – Magyar Biztosítók Évkönyve (Hungarian Insurers' Yearbook) and member list
why_relevant: The clearest example in HU of a true association yearbook: annual 'Magyar Biztosítók Évkönyve' PDFs (2024, 2025 editions observed) carrying market data plus the member roster on a dedicated page — 32 members (26 insurers, 3 branches, 3 associations) per the 2024 edition. Bancassurance ties make this the insurance-side counterpart register to the Bankszövetség list.

source_name: HVCA – Magyar Kockázati- és Magántőke Egyesület, Tagok
why_relevant: ~70 members (28 full, 32 associate, 10 individual) categorised by role, incl. an /tagok/category/investors view. Identifies the capital behind Hungarian fintechs and the PE/VC owners that drive consolidation among payment and lending firms; the 30-year jubilee yearbook adds historical deal context.

source_name: European Banking Federation – national member associations directory
why_relevant: EBF unites 33 national banking associations representing ~3,500 banks; the Hungarian Banking Association is the HU member (Levente Kovács named as its Secretary General in EBF contexts). Useful for cross-country benchmarking of HU against peer associations and for EN-language framing of HU sector positions.

source_name: Leaseurope – member associations (Hungarian Leasing Association since 2016)
why_relevant: The Hungarian Leasing Association joined Leaseurope in 2016 and became an associate member of the Hungarian Banking Association in 2018; Leaseurope publishes pan-European leasing statistics in which the HU series can be benchmarked. Confirms the cross-membership graph linking HU associations.

source_name: European Payments Council – list of member organisations
why_relevant: Enumerates national payment-scheme participants and associations across Europe; the payments-specific counterpart to the EBF list and a route to identifying which HU institutions/associations sit in SEPA and instant-payment scheme governance.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Bankszövetségi Krónikák a digitális átállás korszakában (Kovács Levente)
why_relevant: Book-length association chronicle by the Secretary General covering the digital-transition era; contains a 2024 member-institution list and a longitudinal account of sector policy, consolidation and digitalisation milestones — a ready-made historical baseline for the HU banking narrative.

Hungary's leading financial news portal and the de-facto aggregator of bank earnings. Publishes earnings previews (analyst consensus tables), same-day 'gyorsjelentés' write-ups with quarter-by-quarter figures, and covers subsidiary/local-entity results that never get an English release. Article dates act as reliable timestamps for when a disclosure hit the market.

Where listed-bank (OTP, and BSE-listed financials) earnings previews, analyst consensus numbers and post-results share reaction pieces are published. Consensus tables ahead of a gyorsjelentés are a useful early-warning signal that a disclosure is imminent.

Aggregated analytical output; useful pointer to broker/analyst houses (Concorde, Erste, OTP Elemzési Központ, Equilor) whose research on Hungarian banks is otherwise hard to see. Snowballing analyst bylines here yields further actor/source candidates.

source_name: Portfolio.hu — bank/insurer ranking series ('bankok és biztosítók rangsora')
why_relevant: Recurring (roughly annual, early June, keyed to the 31 May statutory annual-account filing deadline) structured league table built from Hungarian banks' and insurers' filed annual accounts. This is one of the few places where balance-sheet-total and profit rankings across ALL Hungarian banks — including small/foreign-owned subsidiaries — appear in one comparable table.

Long-running Hungarian business daily. Publishes bank quarterly-result stories with headline figures, analyst consensus previews before OTP gyorsjelentés dates, and sector-aggregate pieces off MNB data. Useful second timestamp source and often reproduces bank press-release content near-verbatim.

Business news portal that covers banking-sector structural data (branch counts, headcount, capital, lending/deposit stocks) alongside results — the kind of operational detail relevant to payments/retail-banking footprint that pure earnings coverage omits.

Major independent weekly's online economy desk. Covers bank sector results with an explicit focus on the political/fiscal overlay (bankadó, extraprofitadó) that distorts reported Hungarian bank profits — essential context when reading headline earnings numbers.

source_name: Forbes.hu — Bank Power Ranking (by Visa) + Pénz rovat
why_relevant: Annual proprietary ranking of Hungarian banks built on balance-sheet totals plus qualitative scoring of digital maturity, innovation, sustainability and customer-centricity — a rare structured, comparable view of Hungarian banks' digital/payments posture that no regulator publishes. Started 2025; paired with 'A jövő bankja' awards.

Business/financial portal (successor brand in the former Napi/Economx family) that publishes bank-by-bank quarterly result articles and pre-earnings consensus estimates, including for non-listed banks such as MBH. Not on the seed list — discovered by snowballing — and appears to publish results stories on the same day as Portfolio and vg.hu.

High-reach general news site whose economy desk reports bank annual accounts and sector-profit aggregates, and covers management commentary from results press conferences (e.g. MBH beszámoló pieces quoting the CEO). Useful for executive quotes that never appear in the filed report.

Independent newsroom with an economy desk that covers banking-sector profitability and bank levies. Named in the cell definition; useful as an editorially independent cross-check against Index. Its specific bank-earnings coverage was not confirmed by a direct hit in this run, so treat the section URL as unverified pending liveness/relevance check.

source_subtype: comparison portal / advisory with editorial arm
why_relevant: Comparison/advisory site covering products of 30+ Hungarian banks and financial providers; also publishes derived analyses of bank profitability from filed annual accounts (e.g. year-on-year profit change per large bank after the 31 May filing deadline). Doubles as a product/pricing observatory for retail banking and payments products.

Demonstrates the Hungarian media cross-citation network: Portfolio republishes/cites Bankmonitor analyses. Tag pages like this are cheap pointer indexes for discovering which third-party analytics shops feed the Hungarian financial press.

Personal-finance and financial-markets portal that covers bank results, product moves and frequently republishes analyses from Bank360 and similar shops. Adds retail/consumer-side framing of bank performance that pure IR coverage misses.

source_name: Bank360.hu (analytics shop feeding the Hungarian press)
why_relevant: Hungarian fintech/comparison company (Bank360 Zrt., Budapest, operating since 2016) whose market analyses on mortgages, personal loans and savings are widely quoted by Privátbankár, Economx and Piac&Profit. Tracking it gives early sight of numbers that later appear as press stories.

SME-focused Hungarian business magazine; carries banking and payments coverage angled at corporate/SME banking products and financing conditions, a segment underserved by the equity-market-focused outlets. Discovered via snowball, not on the seed list.

Business-economics portal ('a vállalkozások gazdasági iránytűje') publishing independent economic and financial news/analysis. Named in the cell definition; confirmed live as a business/finance outlet, but no bank-earnings-specific article was surfaced in this run — relevance to A1 earnings coverage remains to be validated.

Hungary's leading English-language business outlet (founded 1992, biweekly print + web). Publishes English write-ups of Hungarian bank sector profit data (typically sourced from MNB releases and MTI) — the practical English bridge for figures that only exist in Hungarian primary sources. Section URL inferred from an article path; treat as unverified.
